newsitem.title: USA: Aid may have gone to N. Korea army -U.S. official.
newsitem.headline: Aid may have gone to N. Korea army -U.S. official.

text.p: A U.S. intelligence official said Thursday that North Korea may have diverted humanitarian aid to its military but it was not a significant boost to Pyongyang's military power.
"In some cases we believe that it has happened," Lt. Gen. Patrick Hughes, director of the Defence Intelligence Agency, told the Senate Armed Services Committee.
But he said he did not believe the amount of aid North Korea could have shifted to its military "has been very large and I am not concerned about it from a strategic standpoint."
Even so, Hughes said, "I think it's reprehensible of the North Korean government to have used any kind of humanitarian aid outside the civil sector for their military."
Hughes gave no details at the public hearing of the possible aid diversion.

North Korea said Monday it had only half the grain it needed to feed its people because of two years of crop flooding. U.S. officials said Thursday the United States was likely to respond positively to a World Food Programme appeal for more food aid for North Korea.
